stories.headline: FDA approves AbbVie's Decnupaz for a rare, aggressive blood cancer

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Decnupaz (pivekimab sunirine-pvzy) on May 27 for adults with blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN), an ultra-rare and aggressive blood cancer with limited treatment options.
Approval was supported by the Phase 1/2 CADENZA trial, a multicenter, open-label study in patients with CD123-positive hematologic malignancies including BPDCN.
In newly diagnosed, treatment-naive patients (n=33), the composite complete response rate was 69.7% with a median duration of response of 9.7 months.
Patients with relapsed or refractory disease (n=51) had a composite complete response rate of 15.7%.
Decnupaz is a CD123-directed antibody and alkylating agent conjugate designed to target BPDCN cells.

stories.headline: Record A$8.7B ($6.2B) data-center spend drives Australia's biggest investment jump since 2014

key_facts.fact: Australian companies spent A$8.7 billion ($6.2 billion) building data centers and buying servers in Q1 2026, almost double the level in the final quarter of 2025, per ABS data released Thursday.
Total private investment rose 6.5% to its highest level since 2014, well above the 1% median estimate of economists.
Data-center spending made up almost 17% of all private investment in the quarter, well above any previous period in data going back to 2006.
Private investment in information media and telecommunications jumped 96.1% from the prior quarter to a new sector record, the largest surge of any industry grouping.
Businesses revised their expected 2026-27 capital expenditure up 9.9% from the first estimate, largely citing planned data-center spending.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea holds rate at 2.50% and lifts growth outlook as oil-driven inflation mounts

key_facts.fact: The Bank of Korea held its policy rate steady at 2.50% on Thursday, May 28, the eighth consecutive meeting without a change.
It was the first rate decision under new Governor Shin Hyun-song, who took office on April 21.
The central bank raised its 2026 growth outlook to 2.6%.
Consumer prices accelerated 2.6% in April from a year earlier, the fastest gain in 21 months, driven by rising petroleum costs after the US-Iran conflict.
South Korea's GDP rose 1.7% quarter-on-quarter in the first quarter, nearly double the central bank's February forecast.
Some economists expect the BOK to raise rates at least twice this year, potentially lifting the benchmark to 3.00%.

stories.headline: ByteDance is developing its own data-center CPUs on Arm and RISC-V to feed AI rollout

key_facts.fact: ByteDance is developing its own central processing units to support its growing AI infrastructure, according to a Reuters report on Thursday citing three people familiar with the chip program.

ByteDance is pursuing two parallel design tracks, one based on SoftBank-owned Arm and another on the open-source RISC-V instruction-set architecture, as it weighs which fits its long-term data-center needs.

Intel and AMD, which supply most of ByteDance's server CPUs, have raised data-center processor prices by between 10% and 35% quarter-over-quarter in recent months, prompting ByteDance to accelerate its in-house push.

ByteDance plans to deploy its proprietary CPU in its own servers and data centers to support a massive rollout of agent-based products including its Coze platform; the project remains at an early stage.

The CPU effort comes days after ByteDance agreed earlier in the week to buy millions of Qualcomm ASICs for AI data-center inference and to have Qualcomm help bring its own ASIC design to volume production.

stories.headline: India's C2i Semiconductors tapes out first AI-server power chip, backed by $16.7M round

key_facts.fact: C2i Semiconductors has taped out its first smart power-stage chip for AI servers, aiming to enter the global market for high-performance power management components used in data centers.
The startup is backed by a recent $16.7 million funding round led by Peak XV Partners.
C2i is a Bengaluru-based fabless chip startup founded in 2024 by veterans from Texas Instruments.
The company plans to initially target tier-2 and tier-3 server customers before attempting to break into hyperscaler supply chains dominated by established global firms.

stories.headline: AI coding startup Cognition raises $1B+ at $26B valuation, run-rate revenue hits $492M

key_facts.fact: Cognition, maker of the autonomous AI software engineer Devin, raised more than $1 billion at a $25 billion pre-money valuation, announced May 27, 2026.
The new valuation is roughly $26 billion post-money, up sharply from a $10.2 billion post-money valuation when it closed a $400 million round eight months earlier in September.
Cognition says its run-rate revenue has grown to $492 million, up from $37 million in May 2025.
The round was led by Lux Capital and General Catalyst, with existing investors including Founders Fund and 8VC and new investors Ribbit Capital, Atreides, and Layer Global.

stories.headline: Record-breaking heat dome bakes western Europe, spiking power prices and straining grids

key_facts.fact: A 'heat dome' of warm air from north Africa pushed temperatures well above May norms across western Europe, with the heat wave forecast to last through the week and intensify further.
Temperatures in Germany were forecast as high as 30C, with much of France above 30C during midday peaks, for Thursday, May 28.
German day-ahead power prices jumped 29% on Wednesday, May 27, as the heat wave raised cooling demand while lower wind generation forced reliance on more expensive gas- and coal-fired plants.
German wind power output was forecast to fall 9.7 GW day-on-day to 4.4 GW for Thursday delivery, with residual non-renewable load seen rising 8.2 GW to 23.5 GW.
Cooling degree days, a measure of air-conditioning demand, were at their highest level in decades, with the warm pattern expected to persist through the weekend.
Scientists say human-driven climate change is amplifying such extremes, making heat waves, droughts and floods more intense and frequent.

stories.headline: FAA grounds SpaceX Starship and orders a mishap probe into the V3 booster failure

key_facts.fact: The FAA determined that SpaceX's May 22 Starship Flight 12 launch resulted in a 'mishap' involving the Super Heavy booster as it flew back after stage separation, and ordered a SpaceX-led investigation it will oversee.
SpaceX must pause all further Starship test launches until the investigation is completed and the FAA approves the final report and any corrective actions.

The booster separated normally but suffered an apparent engine failure during the return burn, causing it to tumble toward the Gulf and most likely explode on impact; there were no reports of public injury or property damage.

The grounding diminishes the chance that another Starship test flight occurs before SpaceX's anticipated IPO in mid-June, with a roadshow set for June 4 and an offering that could raise as much as $80 billion.
Despite the booster failure, the upper-stage Starship released 20 mock satellites and ended with a splashdown in the Indian Ocean as planned.

stories.headline: GCHQ chief warns of a 'narrowing window' against China and Russia in first annual lecture

key_facts.fact: GCHQ director Anne Keast-Butler delivered the agency's inaugural annual lecture at Bletchley Park on Wednesday, May 27, warning the UK and allies have only a 'narrowing window' to stay ahead of technology threats from Russia and China.
She accused Russia of 'scaling up its daily hybrid activity' and 'relentlessly targeting critical infrastructure, democratic processes, supply chains and public trust.'
Keast-Butler called for making cyber security '10 times more urgent' and said everyone 'from board rooms to living rooms' has a role to play in national security.
She said 'China is now a science and tech superpower' with sophisticated capabilities across its intelligence, cyber and military agencies.
Keast-Butler said GCHQ has, in the past few months, developed the blueprint for a new national cyber defence capability that will 'hardwire cutting-edge agentic AI into machine speed cyber defence.'

stories.headline: Illinois passes SB 315, first US law to require independent third-party audits of frontier AI

key_facts.fact: The Illinois House gave unanimous 110-0 approval on May 27, 2026 to SB 315, the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act, sending it to Gov. J.B. Pritzker's desk after Senate passage on May 21.

If signed, Illinois would be the third state to set frontier-model standards, following New York's RAISE Act and California's SB 53, and the first to require annual independent third-party audits of safety protocols.

The Act requires large frontier developers to publish and annually update a framework covering catastrophic-risk assessment, mitigations, cybersecurity, internal governance, and risks from internal use, and to report critical safety incidents.
SB 315 goes beyond existing AI legislation from California and New York regulating America's largest AI companies.

stories.headline: Iran says it hit a US base in retaliation as Trump threatens Oman and rejects draft peace deal

key_facts.fact: US forces carried out new 'defensive' strikes on an Iranian naval base and airport in the Strait of Hormuz area late Wednesday, May 27, targeting a military site said to threaten US forces and commercial traffic.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted a US air base in retaliation early Thursday and warned that any further US aggression would draw a 'more decisive' response.
Trump threatened to 'blow up' US ally Oman if it did not agree to his demands over control of the Strait of Hormuz.
The White House dismissed Iran's latest terms and rejected reports of a draft peace deal as a 'complete fabrication'; Trump said Iran was 'negotiating on fumes.'

The Israeli military declared all areas south of Lebanon's Zahrani River, roughly 25 miles from the border and including Tyre, as 'combat zones' and ordered residents to evacuate ahead of strikes on Hezbollah.
An Israeli soldier was killed by a Hezbollah drone near the Lebanon border, bringing the number of Israeli troops killed in the war with the group to 23.

stories.headline: JD.com founder vows to protect 900,000 workers from being replaced by AI and robots

key_facts.fact: JD.com founder Liu Qiangdong vowed in an internal speech on May 27 to prevent the e-commerce firm's 900,000-strong workforce from losing their jobs to automation.
Liu said the company will 'do everything possible to safeguard employment' and that 'JD.com will not fire a single front-line worker replaced by machines.'
JD has set up more than 80 training bases ('robobase') around the country to retrain blue-collar workers in skills such as maintenance and servicing of automated systems.
The pledge follows a Chinese court ruling in late April that companies cannot terminate employees or cut their salaries just to replace them with AI systems.
JD already runs a fully automated warehouse, opened in 2018, that handles 200,000 orders a day with just four human employees who service the robots.

stories.headline: Mistral signs AI deals with Airbus and BMW, pressing Europe's case for tech sovereignty

key_facts.fact: French AI firm Mistral announced partnerships with carmaker BMW and aerospace company Airbus on May 28, 2026, aiming to grow by linking with defence and industry giants.

Mistral signed a five-year partnership with Airbus to apply AI to defence, space and helicopter manufacturing, including flight safety in the cockpit and aircraft design via digital simulation; the contract value was not disclosed.

Under the Airbus agreement, Airbus will buy licences for Mistral AI's full product suite for on-premises and trusted-cloud deployment across commercial aircraft, helicopter, defence and space activities, with strict security and sovereignty requirements.

For BMW, Mistral will build models that 'understand the physics' of vehicles to optimise crash-test procedures; Mistral also announced a 10-megawatt compute deal with Digital Realty, against four-billion-euro European data-centre plans.
Mistral framed the push as accelerating AI superintelligence development to secure Europe's independence from US tech giants.

stories.headline: OpenAI Foundation commits initial $250M to help workers and economies navigate AI disruption

key_facts.fact: The non-profit that controls OpenAI said on May 27, 2026 it will commit an initial $250 million for grants, partnerships and direct work to help workers and economies navigate AI-driven disruption — its first such commitment.

The funds will back labor-market research, support workers and communities facing near-term displacement, and explore ways to distribute AI's economic gains more broadly; first initiatives are due later in the year.

Longer-term, the foundation wants to turn policy ideas into testable designs, including shifting taxation from labor toward capital, windfall mechanisms, and sovereign wealth funds modeled on Norway's pension fund and Alaska's Permanent Fund.

The OpenAI Foundation received a 26% stake in OpenAI's for-profit entity last year, valued at $130 billion at the time, and in March committed to investing at least $1 billion through the non-profit over the next year.

stories.headline: Orbital Industries raises $50M Series B for AI-designed materials and data-center cooling

key_facts.fact: Orbital Industries, a startup using AI to design advanced materials, raised a $50 million Series B led by Plural, announced May 28, 2026.
Nvidia's venture arm NVentures, a prior investor, joined the round along with returning investors Radical Ventures, Compound and Fly Ventures.

The London- and San Francisco-based company (formerly Orbital Materials) used its AI platform to develop a PFAS-free dielectric cooling fluid and a modular data-center system for next-generation GPUs, via a multi-year partnership with AWS.

Its underlying engine Orb, an AI model for simulating atoms' quantum-mechanical behavior, can simulate 100,000 atoms on a single GPU and runs 10x faster than models from Microsoft and Meta, per independent benchmarks cited by the company.

Orbital Industries was founded in 2022 by Jonathan Godwin (who spent nearly a decade at DeepMind), James Gin-Pollock and Daniel Miodovnik, and employs 50 people; Plural partner Ian Hogarth led the investment.

stories.headline: Salesforce's Agentforce ARR passes $1.2B, up 205%, as agentic revenue tops $1B for first time

key_facts.fact: Salesforce reported Agentforce annual recurring revenue of $1.2 billion, up 205% year-over-year, in Q1 FY2027 results announced May 27, 2026.
Agentforce annualized revenue crossed the $1 billion mark for the first time, with combined AI and data ARR reaching about $3.4 billion.
Salesforce processed 28.6 trillion tokens in the quarter, up 152% quarter-over-quarter, and delivered 3.8 billion agentic work units for customers.

The company signed a record 98 deals worth over $1 million in new ACV in Q1, including a new $72 million enterprise license agreement with the US Air Force, and raised full-year revenue guidance to $45.9-$46.2 billion.

stories.headline: Chip-design software maker Synopsys settles with Elliott, adds Jesse Cohn to board

key_facts.fact: Synopsys announced on May 27 a cooperation agreement with activist investor Elliott Investment Management, appointing Elliott's Jesse Cohn to its board as an independent director effective June 1, 2026.
With Cohn joining, the Synopsys board expands to 11 members, and he will also serve on the Corporate Governance and Nominating Committee.
The cooperation agreement, signed May 26, caps Elliott's stake at 4.9% beneficial ownership and 7.5% aggregate economic exposure, and requires it to keep at least a 1.5% net-long position.
Elliott disclosed a multibillion-dollar stake in Synopsys in March 2026, arguing the chip-design software maker has room to boost sales and improve margins.

stories.headline: Taiwan tech firms complete record $14.5B in debt deals to fund AI capacity buildout

key_facts.fact: Taiwanese tech firms have completed a record $14.5 billion of debt deals so far this year to meet soaring demand for AI capacity, according to Bloomberg data published May 27.
Convertible bond sales from Taiwanese firms hit a record $4.4 billion in the first quarter of 2026 alone, nearly a third of the broader $14.5 billion total.
Cloud server maker Wiwynn led the surge by raising $2 billion; it supplies hardware to operators such as Microsoft and Meta.
Hon Hai (Foxconn) has an up-to-$1.5 billion convertible bond in the pipeline to fund overseas materials procurement, following a $1.1 billion-equivalent loan in February.

AI-server maker Giga Computing launched its first syndicated loan to raise about $1 billion, while memory-controller supplier Phison wrapped up a $400 million facility in about a month, faster than usual.

stories.headline: Tensormesh raises $20M from Nvidia, AMD and CoreWeave to cut AI inference waste

key_facts.fact: Tensormesh raised $20 million, announced May 27, 2026, with participation from Nvidia, AMD and CoreWeave alongside Valley Capital Partners and Laude Ventures.
The company's technology makes AI inference more efficient by eliminating redundant computations; the round brings its total raised to $24.5 million.
The funding coincides with the launch of its flagship software-as-a-service offering, Tensormesh Inference, and will expand hardware integrations with AMD, Nvidia and CoreWeave.
Tensormesh remains committed to the underlying open-source LMCache project.

stories.headline: TSMC reportedly eyes up to 15% 3nm price hike in 2H26 amid AI and ASIC demand

key_facts.fact: TSMC is expected to raise 3nm pricing again in the second half of 2026, with increases of up to 15%, followed by a potential additional 5%-10% hike in 2027, according to Commercial Times sources.
Monthly 3nm capacity at TSMC's main Fab 18 rose from around 130,000 wafers in early 2026 to roughly 160,000-175,000 wafers in the second quarter, yet AI demand still far exceeds expectations.
Utilization at Fab 18 remains elevated with customer queues showing little sign of easing, driving the tightness in advanced-process capacity.
TSMC's annual shareholder meeting on June 4 is expected to draw attention, with Chairman C.C. Wei likely to update on AI demand, advanced processes and overseas expansion.
